chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Rene Hernandez, arranger from Cuba
summary: Rene Hernandez changed the band, arranging with an authentic Cuban feel for Julio Cuevas and others.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Ah - ha, so what do you remember about that time period when Rene came in and Joe Loco was gone?

Well, imagine! There was ahh - the band changed because Rene being a very talented arranger, know, in a way that he was better than anybody. He just went to the bottome of the Cuban music and he was arranging for the best in Cuba. Julio Cuevas - that he was with Cascarita - a great singer, Cuban singer, was singing with him and he was arranging for Cascarita; so he had all the detail that we had to explain to the American arranger here. To Renee, we didn't have to say anything. We used to give him the lead sheet and he take home and when he brought it was something beautiful.
Okay, who was Rene playing with when you sent for him?
Julio Cuevas. Who else had Rene worked for?
Well, practically with everyone because he was such a good musician.
Can you give me some of the names of the bands he worked with?
I think he worked with Casino de la Playa, a little time and with a few other bands and a charanga because he was all around.
And Julio Cuevas had a very popular band at that time?
Oh, yes, one of the best.
I see. Did they record Julio Cuevas?
